subject: biology
title: Cancer
key_idea: Cancer is the result of changes in cells that lead to uncontrolled cell division. The cells form a lump called a tumour. Malignant tumours invade other tissues and spread around the body. Benign tumours stay in one place.

blocks.text: Cancer is a non-communicable disease. It starts when changes in a cell lead to uncontrolled growth and division.

items.meaning: A change in a cell's DNA or genes.
A lump of abnormal cells formed by uncontrolled cell division.
Something that can damage DNA and cause cancer.

items: Mutations happen in the nucleus of a cell.
A mutation can stop the cell dividing in a controlled way.
The cell divides by mitosis again and again and never stops.
A mass of cells forms: a tumour.
Cancer is caused by changes (mutations) in cells.
The cells divide uncontrollably by mitosis.
Uncontrolled division forms a tumour.

blocks.text: There are two types of tumour. Only malignant tumours are cancers.

blocks.text: Scientists have found lifestyle risk factors and genetic risk factors for different types of cancer.

items: Smoking: carcinogens in smoke are inhaled into the lungs and increase the risk of lung cancer.
Ionising radiation and UV light from the Sun or sunbeds can damage DNA.
Some viruses can cause tumours to develop.
Obesity is linked to a higher risk of cancer.
There are genetic risk factors for some cancers.
Some people inherit genes that make these cancers more likely.
Carcinogens, ionising radiation and some viruses can cause cancer.

checks.q: Describe what happens to cells when a tumour forms.
checks.a: Cells grow and divide abnormally, or uncontrollably.

checks.q: Explain what is meant by a malignant tumour.
checks.a: Uncontrolled cell division. The cells invade neighbouring tissues. They spread to other parts of the body in the blood.

checks.q: Name two factors that can cause cancer.
checks.a: Any two from: ionising radiation, viruses, carcinogens.

worked_example.question: Describe the similarities and differences between benign tumours and malignant tumours.
answer_points: Similarity: both result from changes in the cell, DNA or genes.
Similarity: both show uncontrolled cell growth or division.
Similarity: both can form a lump of cells.
Similarity: both are made up of abnormal cells.
Difference: malignant tumours are made of cancer cells. Benign tumours are made of cells that are more similar to normal cells.
Difference: malignant tumours usually grow faster.
Difference: malignant tumours invade neighbouring tissues. Benign tumours do not.
Difference: malignant tumour cells can spread to other parts of the body, in the blood. Benign tumours stay in one place.
Difference: malignant tumours can form secondary tumours. Benign tumours do not.
worked_example.tip: Any four points score one mark each. Give both similarities and differences, or the maximum is three marks.

worked_example.question: Cancer Research UK found that many people do not realise that obesity is linked to an increased risk of developing cancer. In the body, fat tissue sends signals that cause other cells to divide. Describe how this could cause cancer to develop.
answer_points: The cells are triggered to divide by mitosis.
This division is uncontrolled. The cells will not stop dividing, or divide faster.
It creates a mass or large number of cells: a tumour.
worked_example.tip: Link the three steps in order: more cell division, which is uncontrolled, forming a tumour.

worked_example.question: Cancer is caused by changes in cells. Describe the effects that cancer has on cells.
answer_points: The cells grow or divide in an uncontrolled way (a change in the rate of growth or division is allowed).
worked_example.tip: "Grow" on its own is ignored. Say the growth or division is uncontrolled.
